Overview
Rainmaker
Worldwide Inc. (“Rainmaker,” “RAKR,” or the “Company”) is a Nevada corporation focused on commercializing
decentralized water production, purification and wastewater treatment solutions. The Company’s strategy includes atmospheric water
generation systems and water treatment technologies accessed through its relationship with Rainmaker Worldwide Inc., an Ontario corporation
(“RWI”), operating as Miranda Water Technologies, and other technology partners. RWI and its Miranda operations are important
to the Company’s product offering and distribution strategy, particularly in the United States and Mexico. The Company has generated
limited revenues and continues to focus on business development and project execution.
Corporate
History and Structure
The
Company was formerly known as Gold and Silver Mining of Nevada, Inc. On July 3, 2017, the Company completed a reverse merger with RWI,
pursuant to which RWI’s shareholders obtained control of the Company and RWI became a wholly owned (100%) subsidiary of the Company.
Following the transaction, the Company continued under the name Rainmaker Worldwide Inc.
The
Company is subject to the periodic reporting requirements of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934.
Relationship
with Rainmaker Worldwide Inc. (Ontario) and Miranda
RWI
was established in 2014 to commercialize water production and purification technologies. Effective April 1, 2023, the Company divested
a 60% ownership interest in RWI, retaining a 40% interest at that time. On January 22, 2024, RWI acquired a 60% ownership interest in
Miranda Environmental and Water Treatment Technologies (“Miranda”), based in Ankara, Turkey. Miranda’s water purification
and wastewater treatment technologies expanded the product portfolio available to RAKR through its distribution relationship with RWI.
RAKR
works with RWI, operating as Miranda Water Technologies, to market and distribute water production, purification and wastewater treatment
systems. Subsequent to the 2025 fiscal year-end, the parties entered into a new Master Distributor Agreement dated April 30, 2026, which
superseded and replaced the June 1, 2024 Master Distributor Agreement. The new agreement grants RAKR exclusive direct-sales rights in
the United States, subject to limitations that permit other Miranda distributors to operate in the same territory. RAKR may request approval
to pursue opportunities outside the United States, excluding Mexico, on a client-by-client basis. The agreement has an initial five-year
term, subject to earlier termination, including termination by either party on 90 days’ written notice. These commercial rights
are separate from RAKR’s minority investment in RWI. The agreement is filed as Exhibit 10.8 to this Annual Report.
Restructuring
and Impairment of Investment
On
January 16, 2024, the Company invested $400,000 in RWI. On December 31, 2024, the remaining investment balance was reduced through the
settlement of certain obligations, and the balance was converted into additional common shares of RWI. At December 31, 2024, the Company
held a 14.4% ownership interest in RWI. Further dilution reduced that interest to 11.67% at December 31, 2025.
The
Company fully impaired its investment in RWI in 2024 due to RWI’s financial condition at that time. The investment remained recorded
at zero at December 31, 2025. The Company has no decision-making rights in RWI and retains its contractual distribution rights for Miranda
products.
Products
and Services
Atmospheric
Water Generation and Water Treatment
Rainmaker’s
core business focus is decentralized potable water production and purification. The Company’s solutions include:
●
Atmospheric
Water Generation (AWG) systems that produce potable water from ambient humidity using energy-efficient cooling and condensation
processes.
●
Water
purification and wastewater treatment systems supplied through RWI and its Miranda operations, together with complementary technologies
available from other technology partners.
These
systems are designed for modular and scalable deployment, particularly in regions with limited or unreliable water infrastructure. Under
optimal climatic conditions, AWG units are capable of producing up to approximately 5,000 liters of potable water per unit per day.
Rainmaker’s
systems are intended to be deployable using grid power, renewable energy sources, or hybrid configurations, depending on site conditions.
Business
Model and Distribution Strategy
The
Company’s business model is centered on partnerships with local distributors, engineering firms, and project developers who are
responsible for installation, operation, and maintenance of deployed systems. Rainmaker generally works with customers and their contractors
to integrate its systems into broader infrastructure projects.
In
certain markets, including Mexico, the Company collaborates with partners that possess experience in drilling, civil works, logistics,
and mechanical engineering, allowing Rainmaker to participate in comprehensive water project proposals without maintaining large internal
operational teams.
On
June 23, 2025, the Company, RWI and a local partner established RAKR México S.A. de C.V. (“RMEX”) to pursue water
and related commercial opportunities in Mexico. The Company holds an 18.5% direct ownership interest, RWI holds 25.5%, and the local
partner holds 56.0%. The local partner manages RMEX’s day-to-day activities. The Company has no representation on RMEX’s
board and does not control its operations. During 2025, RMEX’s activities were limited to incorporation and administrative setup.
Future
growth is expected to be driven primarily through independent distributors and project-based deployments rather than direct infrastructure
ownership.
Market
Opportunity
Access
to clean and reliable water remains a critical global challenge, particularly in regions with limited infrastructure, growing populations,
or water scarcity. Atmospheric water generation and decentralized water treatment technologies represent potential alternatives to traditional
water sourcing methods in certain applications. Global demand for potable water is expected to increase due to population growth, urbanization,
industrial activity, and climate-related pressures. The Company believes that decentralized water technologies may be suited for select
residential, commercial, industrial, and humanitarian use cases where traditional water supply solutions are impractical or uneconomical.
Suppliers
and Technology Partners
Rainmaker
does not manufacture its core equipment. Principal sources of water purification and wastewater treatment equipment include RWI, operating
as Miranda Water Technologies, and its Miranda operations in Turkey. The Company also relies on other technology partners for complementary
systems. These supplier and distribution relationships are important to the Company’s ability to offer integrated water solutions.
Competition
The
water production and treatment markets are competitive and include numerous domestic and international companies with substantially greater
financial, technical, and operational resources than the Company. Competitors may offer alternative technologies, including desalination,
traditional purification systems, and other decentralized solutions.
Competitive
factors include cost, energy efficiency, regulatory compliance, financing capability, and project execution expertise. The Company believes
its technologies may be competitive in certain niche applications; however, there can be no assurance that it will be able to compete
successfully.
Government
Regulation
Water
production, purification, and distribution activities are subject to varying regulatory requirements depending on jurisdiction. These
regulations may include water quality standards, environmental permitting, construction approvals, and operational licensing.
The
Company seeks to comply with applicable local regulations and, where relevant, international water quality standards, including World
Health Organization guidelines, through its technology partners and distributors.
Intellectual
Property
The
Company relies on contractual distribution and commercialization rights for technologies supplied by RWI, its Miranda operations and
other technology partners. Patent and other proprietary rights associated with those technologies may be held by the relevant technology
owners. The Company’s minority ownership interest in RWI does not constitute direct ownership of those patents or other intellectual
property.
Executive
and Consulting Resources
Rainmaker
operates with a limited internal workforce. Executive management and financial leadership are provided through consulting agreements.
The Company supplements its internal resources through external legal, accounting, and advisory service providers.
